transcript: New York, New York officially opened up on Broadway today. So I will explain the mysterious costume change that happened during the preview period for New York, New York. Now, the musical takes place in the 19 forties, but when I saw it, they ended the show in these contemporary costumes. Originally, during the first week of previews, after the big finale number, you got this little button. Right before the end, these digital screens came down from the ceiling. Everybody dressed up in contemporary clothes, and we were all of a sudden transported to modern day Times Square, New York. New York is full of these movement transitions, and this was no different. You got the contemporary movement of a modern day New York. And in that bustle of the city, our 2 romantic leads bump into each other. And the timelessness of their love stories repeated in modern day. It was cute. It was completely unnecessary. And ultimately they cut it a few days after I saw it. Is one of the reasons why reviewers can't fully review a show in previews, because a lot of things can rapidly change, like cutting out an entire scene and costumes and set pieces before the opening of your show.
